newsitem.title: CANADA: Norcen wins 14 tracts in U.S. Gulf bidding.
newsitem.headline: Norcen wins 14 tracts in U.S. Gulf bidding.

text.p: Norcen Energy Resources Ltd won 14 exploration tracts in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico -- including two in the deep water region -- in Wednesday's federal auction, a Norcen spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Calgary-based Norcen, one of several international oil companies that combined for a record number of bids for rights to drill off the Louisiana coast, paid a total of US$8 million for the acreage, Norcen's Cheryl Dick told Reuters.
"We were happy with the outcome on it," Dick said. "We ended up winning 14 tracts, 12 of them in the shallow water close to our current operations and two in the deep water."
The deep water tracts, Green Canyon 281 and Mississippi Canyon 243, were the the company's first foray into bidding for acreage in the red-hot region.
Norcen had previously farmed-in on deep water acreage lands held by Royal Dutch/Shell Group unit Shell offshore Inc and expected to drill a well there in late 1997 or early 1998, she said.
Norcen's partner in the Green Canyon tract is France's Elf Aquitaine. Each has a 50 percent interest.
Norcen has a 65 percent stake in Mississippi Canyon. Its partners in the acreage include Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd and Spinnaker Royalty Co.
Dick said the shallow water rights picked up were concentrated around Norcen's main central Gulf operating area of Eugene Island.

On Wednesday, a record 1,790 bids for rights to drill in federal waters were unsealed in New Orleans. Producers ended up spending a total of US$1.24 billion for the rights, making the sale the most active since 1985 in terms of dollars bid.
